# Appendix Z: Targeted CNS Subsetting, Local Variance Modeling, and Inter-Tissue Canalization Analysis

This final section of the pipeline focuses on the isolation of the Central Nervous System (CNS) from a single biological replicate (TDR71) to avoid inter-individual confounding factors. It details the local variance modeling, functional characterization, and spatial projection of the CNS subset. Finally, it executes the comparative inter-tissue analysis to evaluate the canalization of gene expression variability across distinct anatomical structures.

## 1. CNS Isolation and Local Variance Modeling

Targeted neural cell types are extracted from the global dataset. The isolated subset undergoes a dedicated normalization and variance modeling procedure to accurately capture intra-tissue stochasticity.

```{r cns_isolation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load required analytical packages
library(Seurat)
library(scran)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Dr.eg.db)

# Define the targeted central nervous system (CNS) cell types based on anatomical ontology
cns_cell_types <- c(
  "neuronal stem cell",
  "glial cell",
  "radial glial cell", 
  "oligodendrocyte",
  "midbrain interneuron",
  "neuroblast"
)

# Subset the global Seurat object to isolate CNS cells from a single biological replicate (TDR71)
seurat_cns_tdr71 <- subset(
  x = seurat_filtre, 
  subset = fish == "TDR71" & zebrafish_anatomy_ontology_class %in% cns_cell_types
)

# Convert the localized subset to the SingleCellExperiment (SCE) framework
sce_cns_tdr71 <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_cns_tdr71)

# Perform local Quality Control and Normalization specifically for the CNS subset
set.seed(100)
clusters_cns <- quickCluster(sce_cns_tdr71)
sce_cns_tdr71 <- computeSumFactors(sce_cns_tdr71, cluster = clusters_cns)
sce_cns_tdr71 <- logNormCounts(sce_cns_tdr71)

# Model local gene expression variance within the isolated neural tissue
dec_cns_tdr71 <- modelGeneVar(sce_cns_tdr71)

# Extract local Highly Variable Genes (HVGs) representing the top 10% of biological variance
hvg_cns_tdr71 <- getTopHVGs(dec_cns_tdr71, prop = 0.10)
VariableFeatures(seurat_cns_tdr71) <- hvg_cns_tdr71

print(paste("Number of cells in the CNS subset:", ncol(seurat_cns_tdr71)))
print(paste("Number of local HVGs identified (top 10%):", length(hvg_cns_tdr71)))

# Visualize and export the localized scran variance model
pdf("Scran_Variability_TDR71.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
plot(dec_cns_tdr71$mean, dec_cns_tdr71$total, 
     xlab = "Mean expression (log)", 
     ylab = "Total variance", 
     main = "scran Model - CNS Local Variability (TDR71)",
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "darkgrey")
curve(metadata(dec_cns_tdr71)$trend(x), col = "blue", add = TRUE, lwd = 2)
dev.off()
```

##2. Functional Characterization (Gene Ontology) of Local CNS Variability
To interpret the biological significance of the local variance, a Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis is performed strictly on the CNS HVGs.

```{r cns_isolation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Extract the previously defined CNS HVGs and define the specific background universe
hvg_cns_genes <- VariableFeatures(seurat_cns_tdr71)
cns_universe <- rownames(seurat_cns_tdr71)

# Perform GO enrichment targeting Biological Processes (BP)
ego_cns <- enrichGO(
  gene          = hvg_cns_genes,
  keyType       = "SYMBOL",
  OrgDb         = org.Dr.eg.db,
  ont           = "BP",                 
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",                 
  universe      = cns_universe,         
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.05
)

# Export the raw enrichment results as a tabular text file for record-keeping
cns_txt = data.frame(ego_cns)
cns_txt1 = data.frame(cns_txt$ID, cns_txt$p.adjust)
write.table(cns_txt1, file="cns_GO_BP.txt", row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, sep="\t", quote=FALSE)

# Generate and export the functional enrichment dotplot if significant terms are identified
if (!is.null(ego_cns) && nrow(as.data.frame(ego_cns)) > 0) {
  dotplot_cns <- dotplot(ego_cns, showCategory = 15) + 
    ggtitle("Functional Enrichment of Local CNS HVGs (TDR71)")
  print(dotplot_cns)
  
  pdf("GO_Enrichment_CNS_Local.pdf", width = 12, height = 8)
  print(dotplot_cns)
  dev.off()
} else {
  print("No statistically significant GO terms found.")
}
```

##3. Local Dimensionality Reduction & Spatial Mapping
The CNS subset undergoes an independent Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and spatial projection (UMAP) to visualize the intra-tissue cellular heterogeneity.

```{r cns_isolation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Normalize and scale the data specifically for the local neural HVGs
seurat_cns_tdr71 <- NormalizeData(seurat_cns_tdr71)
seurat_cns_tdr71 <- ScaleData(object = seurat_cns_tdr71, features = hvg_cns_tdr71)

# Execute Principal Component Analysis (PCA) restricted to the local subset
seurat_cns_tdr71 <- RunPCA(object = seurat_cns_tdr71, features = hvg_cns_tdr71, npcs = 15)

# Compute the UMAP projection based on the top 10 local PCs
seurat_cns_tdr71 <- RunUMAP(object = seurat_cns_tdr71, dims = 1:10)

# Visualize and export the localized UMAP colored by neural cell subtypes
umap_cns_local <- DimPlot(
  object = seurat_cns_tdr71, 
  reduction = "umap", 
  group.by = "zebrafish_anatomy_ontology_class", 
  label = TRUE, 
  repel = TRUE,
  pt.size = 2
) + ggtitle("Local UMAP: CNS Cell Types (TDR71)")

ggsave("UMAP_CNS_Cell_Types_TDR71.pdf", plot = umap_cns_local, width = 12, height = 8)
```

##4. Intra-CNS Variability Exploration
Biological variance is modeled and compared internally across the distinct neural cell types to quantify differentiation plasticity.

```{r cns_isolation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Model gene variance blocked by specific neural cell types
dec_cns_per_type <- modelGeneVar(sce_cns_tdr71, block = sce_cns_tdr71$zebrafish_anatomy_ontology_class)
cns_blocks <- dec_cns_per_type$per.block
bio_var_list_cns <- list()

# Extract and format the variance data for each cell type
for (cell_type in names(cns_blocks)) {
  bio_var_list_cns[[cell_type]] <- data.frame(
    Gene = rownames(cns_blocks[[cell_type]]),
    Bio_Variance = cns_blocks[[cell_type]]$bio,
    Cell_Type = cell_type
  )
}
df_cns_bio_var <- do.call(rbind, bio_var_list_cns)

# Generate and export boxplots illustrating variance distributions per neural subtype
boxplot_cns_types <- ggplot(df_cns_bio_var, aes(x = Cell_Type, y = Bio_Variance, fill = Cell_Type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Biological Variability Across CNS Cell Types",
    x = "CNS Cell Type", 
    y = "Biological Variance (scran 'bio')"
  )

ggsave("Biological_variability_CNS.pdf", plot = boxplot_cns_types, width = 12, height = 8)
```

##5. Peripheral Normalization & Inter-Tissue Canalization Analysis
To evaluate inter-tissue expression constraints, peripheral tissues (liver, fin, muscle) are isolated and normalized. A dynamic comparative analysis is then executed to track the variance of focal HVGs across non-target tissues, validating the canalization hypothesis.

```{r cns_isolation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggpubr) # Required for non-parametric statistical annotations

# Isolate peripheral tissues from the same biological replicate
peripheral_tissues <- c("liver", "fin", "muscle")
seurat_periph <- subset(seurat_filtre, subset = fish == "TDR71" & zebrafish_anatomy_ontology_class %in% peripheral_tissues)
sce_periph <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_periph)

# Perform strict Quality Control and Normalization for peripheral cell populations
set.seed(100)
clusters_periph <- quickCluster(sce_periph)
sce_periph <- computeSumFactors(sce_periph, cluster = clusters_periph)
sce_periph <- logNormCounts(sce_periph)

# Model variance utilizing the specific peripheral tissue as a blocking factor
dec_periph <- modelGeneVar(sce_periph, block = sce_periph$zebrafish_anatomy_ontology_class)
block_stats <- dec_periph$per.block

# Extract the top 10% HVGs independently for each peripheral tissue
indiv_hvgs <- lapply(block_stats, function(x) {
  top_genes <- getTopHVGs(x, prop = 0.10)
  x[top_genes, "bio", drop = FALSE]
})

# Compile the global list of focal HVGs by appending the Brain (CNS) subset
indiv_hvgs[["Brain (CNS)"]] <- dec_cns_tdr71[hvg_cns_tdr71, "bio", drop = FALSE]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dynamic Generation of Inter-Tissue Statistical Boxplots
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
tissues_to_plot <- c("Brain (CNS)", "liver", "fin", "muscle")

# Define strict statistical comparisons (Brain vs. all other peripheral tissues)
my_comparisons <- list(
  c("Brain (CNS)", "liver"),
  c("Brain (CNS)", "fin"),
  c("Brain (CNS)", "muscle")
)

# Iterate over each tissue to evaluate the constraint of its specific HVGs elsewhere
for (source_tissue in tissues_to_plot) {
  
  # 1. Isolate focal HVGs for the currently evaluated tissue
  current_hvgs <- rownames(indiv_hvgs[[source_tissue]])
  comparison_list <- list()
  
  # 2. Extract matching variance values from the Brain (CNS) dataset
  cns_matched <- rownames(dec_cns_tdr71)[rownames(dec_cns_tdr71) %in% current_hvgs]
  comparison_list[["Brain (CNS)"]] <- data.frame(
    gene = cns_matched,
    Variance = dec_cns_tdr71$bio[rownames(dec_cns_tdr71) %in% current_hvgs],
    Tissue = "Brain (CNS)",
    HVG_Source = rep(source_tissue, length(cns_matched))
  )
  
  # 3. Extract matching variance values from the Peripheral datasets
  for (periph_tiss in peripheral_tissues) {
    if (periph_tiss %in% names(block_stats)) {
      periph_matched <- rownames(block_stats[[periph_tiss]])[rownames(block_stats[[periph_tiss]]) %in% current_hvgs]
      comparison_list[[periph_tiss]] <- data.frame(
        gene = periph_matched,
        Variance = block_stats[[periph_tiss]]$bio[rownames(block_stats[[periph_tiss]]) %in% current_hvgs],
        Tissue = periph_tiss,
        HVG_Source = rep(source_tissue, length(periph_matched))
      )
    }
  }
  
  # 4. Merge all targeted variance data into a unified dataframe
  df_tissue_plot <- do.call(rbind, comparison_list)
  
  # 5. Generate independent boxplots with structured statistical annotations
  p <- ggplot(df_tissue_plot, aes(x = Tissue, y = Variance, fill = Tissue)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    theme_bw() +
    
    # Expand the y-axis ceiling to properly accommodate staggered significance brackets
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.2, 3)) + 
    
    # Apply Wilcoxon rank-sum test with forced staggered y-positions for readability
    stat_compare_means(
      comparisons = my_comparisons,
      method = "wilcox.test",
      label = "p.signif",
      label.y = c(1.8, 2.0, 2.2), 
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = paste("Variability of", source_tissue, "HVGs Across Tissues"),
      subtitle = paste("Assessing the canalization of", source_tissue, "transcriptomic networks"),
      x = "Tissue Evaluated", 
      y = paste("Biological Variance of", source_tissue, "HVGs"),
      caption = "Wilcoxon rank-sum test vs Brain (CNS) \n ns: p > 0.05 | *: p <= 0.05 | **: p <= 0.01 | ***: p <= 0.001 | ****: p <= 0.0001"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, margin = margin(b = 15)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 13, color = "black"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "italic", size = 12, color = "gray30", margin = margin(t = 15))
    )
  
  print(p)
  
  # 6. Sanitize filenames and export the final visualizations to PDF
  safe_filename <- gsub(" |\\(\vert{}\\)", "_", source_tissue) 
  safe_filename <- gsub("__", "_", safe_filename)
  
  ggsave(
    filename = paste0("Variability_HVG_", safe_filename, "_Across_Tissues.pdf"), 
    plot = p, 
    width = 10, 
    height = 7, 
    device = "pdf"
  )
}
```
